cards.text: Friend, pull up a stool. The king of Aram is at war against Israel. After talking it over with his servants, he says, "My camp will be in such and such a place."
But Elisha, the man of God, sends a message to the king of Israel about that exact spot.

cards.question: Elisha sends the king of Israel a message about the spot where Aram plans to camp. What does the message say?

answers.text: Be careful not to pass by that place
Set up your own camp there first
Attack that place before they arrive

cards.question: Elisha warns the king of Israel about Aram's plans only one time.

cards.text: Time and again, Aram picks a spot and Israel's king is already on guard there. That's like planning a surprise party for a guy who's IN the group chat.

cards.question: Every plan the king of Aram makes keeps getting blocked, and he's enraged. Who does he think is behind it?

answers.text: Scouts from Israel on the hills

cards.text: One of the servants answers, "No one, my lord the king." The leak is Elisha, the prophet in Israel.

cards.question: The servant says Elisha tells the king of Israel the very words the king of Aram speaks in his ___.

cards.text: His BEDROOM! Now the king of Aram wants Elisha found, so he can send men to capture him.

cards.question: The report comes back to the king of Aram. Where is Elisha?
To capture Elisha, the king of Aram sends horses, chariots and a great ___.

cards.text: All that for ONE prophet? That's calling the fire department to blow out a birthday candle.
They go by night and surround the city. Early in the morning, Elisha's servant goes outside and sees an army with horses and chariots all around the city.

cards.question: When Elisha's servant sees the army around the city, he asks Elisha what they are going to do.
Elisha tells his servant not to be afraid. What reason does he give?

answers.text: There are more with us than with them
The army will leave before night
The city walls are too strong for them

cards.text: More with US? I bet that servant counted the two of them and started sweating.
Then Elisha prays, "O LORD, please open his eyes that he may see."

cards.question: The LORD opens the young man's eyes, and he sees the hills full of horses and chariots of ___ all around Elisha.

cards.text: Now the Arameans come down against Elisha. And Elisha prays again.

cards.question: As the Arameans come down against him, what does Elisha ask the LORD to do to them?

answers.text: Put them into a deep sleep

cards.text: The LORD strikes them with blindness, according to the word of Elisha. A whole army that can't see a thing, and after years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, I KNOW that feeling.

cards.question: Elisha speaks to the blinded Arameans. What does he tell them?

answers.text: This is the wrong city so follow me
Lay down your swords and go home
Wait right here until your eyes clear

cards.text: Then he says, "Follow me, and I will take you to the man you are seeking." That's the guy you're looking for offering to help you look for him!

cards.question: Elisha leads the blinded Arameans to a city. Which one?

cards.text: They walk all the way into Samaria. Then Elisha prays one more time.

cards.question: Inside Samaria, Elisha asks the LORD to open the ___ of the Arameans.

cards.text: They look around and discover they're in Samaria. That's dozing off on the train and waking up at the VERY last stop.
The king of Israel sees them and turns to Elisha. He calls him "My father."

cards.question: With the Arameans standing in Samaria, what does the king of Israel ask Elisha?

answers.text: Whether he should keep them as servants
Whether he should send them back blind

cards.text: And he asks it TWICE: "Shall I kill them? Shall I kill them?" That's me at the oven door going, "Are they done? Are they done?"

cards.question: Elisha tells the king of Israel to go ahead and kill the Arameans.
So what does Elisha tell the king of Israel to do with the Arameans instead?

answers.text: Set food and water before them
Lock them up in the city prison
Make them work on the city walls

cards.question: The king of Israel doesn't hold back. He prepares a great ___ for the Arameans.

cards.text: They showed up to capture a prophet and they leave with a FEAST in them. When they finish eating and drinking, the king sends them away, and they go back to their master.

cards.question: After that, the Aramean raiders did not come into the land of Israel again.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 12 quotes "Shall I kill them? Shall I kill them?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card is only a reaction joke ("All that for ONE prophet?..."). It tells nothing new from the passage, because card 11 already covered the army in 2 Kings 6:14. It should carry a piece of the passage, such as the night march and the surrounding of the city (now on card 13), with the joke riding along.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card cites 2 Kings 6:14 but retells nothing from that verse. Its citation doesn't match what the card tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card is only a reaction joke ("More with US? I bet that servant counted..."). Card 15 already covered verse 16, so the card doesn't move the passage forward. The joke could ride on card 17 with Elisha's prayer, or the two cards could be combined.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card cites 2 Kings 6:16 but retells nothing new from that verse. Card 15 already covered it, so the citation doesn't match what this card tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: No card tells or asks about Elisha's reason in 2 Kings 6:22, "Would you kill those you have captured with your own sword or bow?" That reason is the key to why the king spares the Arameans. The baker learns only that Elisha said no and to feed them.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 5 of the 9 choice cards in stop 2, against 2 fill in the blank and 2 true or false. It also fills the first three choice cards in a row (cards 2, 4 and 6).

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
